Restaurante La Casa de Socorro

A favorite among tourists for decades, going back to the days when other Colombians were essentially the only tourists. The quality waned for a while, but a recent revamp has it good again.

Celele

Probably the best foodie experience in Cartagena — very creative dishes with interesting twists on Colombian favorites. For dinner, book ahead of time.

La Esquina del Pandebono

Quick breakfast

This is where we get quick breakfast items. They have an espresso/latte machine, fruit smoothies, a good liquid oatmeal, Milo (a Colombian treat), and great pastries — ask which ones just came out of the oven. It's two long blocks from the apartment along Calle de la Moneda.

🏊Pool Day Passes

Sofitel Legend Santa Clara

Former monastery

Day pass around COP 120,000, of which COP 80,000 goes toward food and drink — subject to availability, which is tighter on weekends. A former monastery and a beautiful hotel, even if just for a drink in the central patio.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Hotel Santa Catalina

Day pass around COP 120,000 on weekends and COP 60,000 on weekdays, all of which goes toward food and drink. A very nice option with great views of the Old City from the rooftop.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Hilton Cartagena

Bocagrande

A great option recommended by a guest. They charge roughly COP 100,000–130,000 per person depending on availability, with access to their four swimming pools and private beach. About 15–20 minutes by taxi from the apartment, in Bocagrande.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Hotel Bantu by Faranda Boutique

A day pass including a sauna runs about COP 180,000, of which COP 80,000 goes toward food and drink. Quirky, with nice rooftop views.

🛍️Shopping

Casa Abba – Gallery-Boutique

My favorite little local gallery — creative, locally designed clothing and accessories, paintings, decorations and more.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Arte Getsemaní Gallery

Getsemaní

A good central point to start seeing Getsemaní's street art — but the best approach is to stop by here while also wandering the streets and taking it all in.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Mallplaza El Castillo

About a 10-minute walk from the apartment toward Castillo San Felipe — a good mall for shopping. Colombia produces good clothing at good prices: Falabella, Arturo Calle and Tennis, among other stores with prices that are affordable for foreigners.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Bazurto Market

The real, local Cartagena market — you'll find everything here. It's chaotic and fun, but visit only if you're comfortable potentially standing out, and keep a very close eye on your valuables.

📍 Open in Google Maps

Pasaje Nueva Colombia

Across the street

Almost directly across from the apartment. You'll find Colombian jerseys and souvenirs, tailors, cobblers, hat sellers and more. Worth walking through for the mix of souvenirs and things locals actually shop for — and if a shirt doesn't fit perfectly, have it tailored right here.

🏝️Sightseeing & Beaches

Playa Blanca

Barú

If you want more beach time, or prefer to skip a guided Islas del Rosario tour, this is where we go when we're craving a beach day. You can get there by private car, which runs about COP 220,000 round trip; or, for more sea time, by boat for roughly COP 100,000 per person.

To go by boat, walk to the marina by the Convention Center and Clock Tower the day before or that morning. Ask the boat companies what they're charging for round-trip rides to Playa Blanca in Barú. Boats leave roughly every 30 minutes — but confirm with the operator before buying a ticket, and make sure you know where and when your boat passes by in the afternoon for the ride back.

The best part of the beach is to the right as you get off the boat. You can rent a chair for the day, relax, and negotiate lunch and drinks — always ask the price first before accepting any food or service like massages, as it's a touristy spot with some pushy vendors.

This is a more do-it-yourself, low-key beach day, and not for everyone. Islas del Rosario is very special, so ideally this is a bonus beach day once you're comfortable getting around Cartagena.

Rosario Islands

Las Islas

“Las Islas” are by far the prettiest beaches near Cartagena, reachable by hiring a boat tour operator. We don't officially endorse one because we haven't yet found one we love and know to be consistent — but here are operators that previous guests have had good experiences with and that may be worth checking out:

Aviario Nacional de Colombia

National Aviary

Many of our guests have visited and loved it, which was our experience as well. Definitely worth reading up on. It's a little over an hour by car from the apartment, and can be combined with a visit to Playa Blanca as well. It's necessary to hire a driver to get here.
